research_concepts: lineup role coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of coverage from role counts
methodological_questions: Does lineup coverage vary across lineups within a team-season beyond what role counts and chance produce?
Is coverage separable from lineup talent and from the number of role-holders?
Does the talent control behave (non-degenerate, not collinear with coverage, not leaking outcomes)?
Are organizer, shaper and terminal labels derived independently of the outcomes they are later related to?

historical_evidence.finding: Team offensive association structure is more similar to itself across split halves than to other teams, even after residualizing play-type rates (Frobenius P1a S=0.352, P1b S=0.353, residual R2=0.043).

Structural influence is not reducible to usage (F1a cosine R2 about 0.09-0.10, residual share about 0.90), and the usage-residual is split-half stable (pooled rho about +0.67-0.69). The record lists low measurement reliability as a limitation.

Real absences move association structure (V1 confirmed, 16/23 above null p95), but the leave-one-out simulation did not predict the magnitude (V2a rho=+0.288, CI [-0.244,+0.667], FAIL). The record lists small sample as a limitation.

An apparent adapter PPP lift was not supported by the falsification tests: wrong-way teams did not do worse than no-signal teams, and there was no next-game carryover. The record attributes the effect to a construction, selection or labelling flaw (label error, regression to the mean, mechanical floor).

Inferred defensive-scheme labels were near-uniform in their transition matrices, which is consistent with label noise. The record says real adjustment cannot be separated from the offense executing differently.
Lineup-matched teammate PPP lift after elite creators' actions was a clean null with adequate power (Jokic lag-1 ATT +0.028, CI [-0.043,+0.099], n=1880).
Star-by-lineup suppression gaps were found with no placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Rank-1 suppressor deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control.
Sequential suppression cells had n_after of 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions, with no multiplicity correction.
Player-channel lifts were large on small cells (n often 15-54), which the record flags as insufficient exposure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Interpreting an adapter PPP lift as a real response using inferred labels, without falsification.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact from label error, regression to the mean and a mechanical floor.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred categorical labels to detect change.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable because of label noise; real change cannot be separated from execution differences.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading effects from small lineup or player cells with no placebo or matching.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts (placebo dependence).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking top-suppressor cells across many players and play types.
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction and small n_after cells.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Decomposing effects into small player-channel cells.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unanswerable because of insufficient exposure.

evidence_establishes: Team-level structural signatures are reproducible across split halves and are only weakly explained by play-type rates (FAM:SF17, supported).
Player-level structural influence is not reducible to usage and is split-half stable (FAM:SF18, supported).

The project has repeatedly recorded artifacts and non-tests from small cells, inferred labels, missing placebos and missing multiplicity control (FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-066).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record defines or tests organizer, shaper and terminal lineup coverage, within-team variation in it, or separability of coverage from talent and role counts.
No retrieved record evaluates a talent control or shows how it behaves.
The records give no information on how role labels are derived or on their reliability.
The records give no information on how many lineups meet minimum-possession thresholds in this dataset.
own_inferences: Coverage is a deterministic function of the role assignment of five players. Variation within team and a dependence on role counts are therefore partly mechanical, and 'separable from counts' needs a null that holds counts fixed (for example within-team permutation of role labels across players).

If roles or talent are derived from the same possessions or outcomes used to evaluate coverage, the talent control can leak. Players who hold more roles are usually also higher-talent, so coverage, counts and talent are likely collinear. 'Talent control behaves' should be treated as a diagnostic with pre-set criteria, not as an assumption.

With about 4,700 possessions per team-season spread over many lineups, most lineups will be thin. Within-team variation estimates need possession weighting or a minimum-exposure gate, and a fixed-effects model on sparse lineups risks inflated variance estimates.
The question bundles three claims. They should be tested and reported separately, with a joint pass only if all three pass.
The project's history of artifacts from label error points to a meaningful chance that apparent coverage effects come from role-label construction.
uncertainties: The operational definitions and thresholds for organizer, shaper and terminal are not given in the task.
The talent measure is not specified (prior-season, same-season or box-based), and neither is the outcome, if any.
The number of lineups per team-season above an exposure threshold is unknown.
Whether roles are stable within a season is unknown, which matters for drift across the four seasons.
I did not read the full text of any retrieved family; some were truncated in the retrieval result.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record tests this question, so prior work did not answer it. The history moved the decision toward proceeding with changes: pre-specified permutation nulls and placebos, an exposure gate, split-half role derivation to avoid label leakage, and multiplicity control. It also lowered my confidence in any unadjusted positive result because of the artifact and label-noise precedents. The supported structural-stability findings (FAM:SF17, FAM:SF18) modestly raise the plausibility that role-based structure is measurable.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels and the talent measure must be shown reliable (split-half) before coverage is interpreted; if labels are noisy, the separability test is uninterpretable.
Lineup-level cells within a team-season are sparse; a minimum-possession gate may leave too few lineups per team for within-team inference.
If roles or talent are built from the same play-by-play outcomes later used to evaluate coverage, the control cannot be said to 'behave'.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family addresses lineup role coverage. Adjacent structural work (FAM:SF17, FAM:SF18) supports stable team and player structure that is not reducible to play-type rates or usage. The project's cautionary history (FAM:SF-APPA-001 artifact, FAM:SF-APPA-005 untestable, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050 and FAM:SF-APPA-066 not hypothesis tests) concerns label noise, small cells and missing placebos.

risks.text: Coverage is determined by the roster composition of each lineup. Within-team variation and dependence on counts arise by construction, so the test needs a count-preserving permutation null.
Talent, role counts, minutes and starter status are collinear with coverage. Lineups with more role-holders are likely better players and play more minutes.
Roles or the talent control derived from the same possessions as the test create circularity.
Same-season role or talent estimates that use later games leak information into earlier lineups; they should be estimated out-of-sample.
Role classification noise (cf. the label-noise records) attenuates coverage differences and can create spurious ones.
The 90 team-seasons give limited power for team-level moderators; the lineup unit has more observations but is clustered within team-season.
Most lineups have few possessions, so coverage per lineup is poorly measured.
Several role definitions, thresholds, seasons and splits multiply the number of tests unless pre-specified.
Role prevalence and lineup construction may change across the four seasons and between regular season and playoffs; the 2025-26 data were partial at some dates.
Without placebo role labels, any structure found may reflect lineup composition generally rather than these roles.

design.estimand: Three separate estimands. (A) Within-team-season, possession-weighted variance of the lineup coverage indicator C (1 if the five-man lineup contains >=1 organizer, >=1 shaper and >=1 terminal), compared with its distribution under a count-preserving permutation null. (B) The incremental share of between-lineup variance in C explained by team-season fixed effects plus the role-count vector plus lineup talent, versus count-only and talent-only models; and the association of C with an outcome (for example lineup PPP), conditional on counts and talent. (C) Talent-control diagnostics: the correlation of talent with C and with counts, the variance inflation factor, and the stability of coefficients when talent is estimated out-of-sample.
design.unit: Lineup within team-season (five-man unit), weighted by possessions; team-season as the cluster.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (complete) as the primary sample, 90 team-seasons. Playoffs and partial 2025-26 playoff data are held out as a secondary sample. Lineups need at least 50 possessions (the threshold is pre-set; sensitivity at 30 and 100). Record the number of lineups and the share of possessions retained per team-season before any inference.
design.power: Compute before analysis: the number of eligible lineups per team-season and the minimum detectable variance ratio under the permutation null, by simulation using the observed exposure distribution. Stop and report 'untestable' for (B) if fewer than about 15 eligible lineups exist in over half of the team-seasons, or if the effective sample after clustering gives a minimum detectable partial R2 above 0.05.
design.controls: Derive roles (organizer, shaper, terminal) from a split of the data that is disjoint from the evaluation possessions (for example odd versus even games, or prior-season data), with thresholds fixed in advance. Estimate talent out-of-sample (prior-season or opposite-half), and exclude outcome-derived measures from any model whose outcome is the same possessions. Include role counts, minutes share, starter share and season. Cluster by team-season.
design.falsification: (1) Within-team permutation of role labels across players, preserving each player's role count and each team's role counts. (2) Placebo role sets with matched prevalence (for example random labels or labels from an unrelated stat) with the same coverage definition. (3) Split-half reliability of role labels; if it falls below a pre-set threshold (for example kappa below 0.6), declare (B) untestable. (4) Check that results hold when the outcome is replaced by a lagged or opposite-half outcome. (5) Verify that the talent control predicts something it should (for example lineup net rating out of sample) without absorbing all variation in C.
design.multiplicity: One primary test per estimand (A, B, C), with Holm correction across the three. Role-threshold, season and playoff-versus-regular analyses are secondary and use Benjamini-Hochberg control; no post-hoc role definitions.
design.decision_rule: Supported if (A) observed within-team variance exceeds the permutation null at Holm-adjusted p<0.05 AND (B) coverage adds incremental variance beyond counts and talent with a CI excluding zero, while the placebo roles show no comparable effect AND (C) the talent control meets pre-set criteria (VIF below 5, correlation with C below 0.7, coefficients stable out-of-sample). Rejected if the CI for (B) is within a pre-set equivalence margin and power is adequate. Artifact if the effect disappears under count-preserving permutation or under placebo roles. Untestable if the reliability or exposure criteria fail. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files (play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, box score) and the derived play-type possession records, for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data snapshot and role-derivation code at pre-registration and record the date; the research question was posed on 2026-07-13.

methodological_questions: Does lineup role coverage vary within team-seasons?
Is coverage separable from talent and role counts?
Does the talent control behave (stable, non-degenerate, no leakage)?
How are organizer, shaper and terminal roles derived, and are the labels outcome-derived?
args.query: lineup coverage of organizer, shaper and terminal roles within team, separability from talent and role counts, behavior of talent control

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
